You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

1	# Crowbook
2	
3	Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.
4	
5	It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.
10	
11	## Installing
12	
13	Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	The simplest invocation is:
18	
19	    $ crowbook <BOOK>
20	
21	where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.
22	
23	For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.
24	
25	## Output formats
26	
27	Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.
28	
29	Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.
30	
31	## Input format
32	
33	Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.
34	
35	## Customization
36	
37	Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.
38	
39	## Bugs and support
40	
41	Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

crowbook 0.17.0 by Élisabeth Henry <liz.henry@ouvaton.org>
Render a Markdown book in EPUB, PDF or HTML.
  
USAGE:
    executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK]

OPTIONS:
  -f, --force-emoji
          Force emoji usage even if it might not work on your system
  -s, --single
          Use a single Markdown file instead of a book configuration file
  -n, --no-fancy
          Disably fancy UI
  -v, --verbose
          Print warnings in parsing/rendering
  -a, --autograph
          Prompts for an autograph for this book
  -q, --quiet
          Don't print info/error messages
  -c, --create <files>...
          Create a new book with existing Markdown files
  -o, --output <output>
          Specify output file
  -t, --to <to>
          Generate specific format
      --set <set> <set>...
          Set a list of book options
  -l, --list-options
          List all possible options
  -L, --lang <lang>
          Set the runtime language used by Crowbook
      --print-template <print-template>
          Prints the default content of a template
  -S, --stats
          Print some project statistics
  -h, --help
          Print help
  -V, --version
          Print version

ARGS:
  [BOOK]  File containing the book configuration file, or a Markdown file when called with --single

+ test.md# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

42 /workspace/README.md
# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

ref
# Crowbook

Crowbook lets you write a book in Markdown and generate HTML, PDF and EPUB output without worrying about formatting or typography.

It focuses on novels and fiction and provides sensible defaults to produce readable books with correct typography.

## Example

To see Crowbook's output examples, see the project's published book pages (HTML, PDF, EPUB) on the project's website or releases.

## Installing

Download a precompiled binary for your platform from the project's releases page and place the executable somewhere on your PATH.

## Usage

The simplest invocation is:

    $ crowbook <BOOK>

where <BOOK> is a book configuration file. Crowbook will parse this file and generate HTML, EPUB, and/or PDF output according to the settings.

For short texts contained in a single Markdown file, Crowbook can accept a single Markdown file with embedded metadata and produce output directly.

## Output formats

Crowbook supports HTML, PDF and EPUB as output formats.

Note: Generating PDF output typically requires a working LaTeX installation (for example, xelatex) on your system.

## Input format

Crowbook accepts CommonMark-like Markdown input. You can also include a small metadata block (YAML) at the top of a single Markdown file to set title/author and other options when running in single-file mode.

## Customization

Templates allow you to customize the visual appearance of the generated books. See the project's documentation for template usage and examples.

## Bugs and support

Report issues on the project's issue tracker (link available on the project's website or GitHub repository page).

args.command:
cat > /workspace/ref/reports/cli.md <<'REPORT_EOF' # AREA: CLI surface — crowbook 0.17.0 (`/workspace/executable`) All tests run on Linux, cwd a scratch dir, stdout/stderr captured separately. Unless noted, both streams were piped (not a tty). Binary name in clap messages is `executable` (argv[0]-dependent). Test fixtures used (created in scratch dir): `ch1.md`: ``` # Chapter One This is a *test* chapter with some words. ``` `ch2.md`: ``` # Chapter Two More words here. And some more. ``` `book.book`: ``` author: Probe Author title: Probe Book lang: en + ch1.md + ch2.md ``` ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## 1. `--help` / `-h` `crowbook --help` → exit 0, everything on STDOUT, STDERR empty. Verbatim: ``` crowbook 0.17.0 by Élisabeth Henry Render a Markdown book in EPUB, PDF or HTML. USAGE: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] OPTIONS: -f, --force-emoji Force emoji usage even if it might not work on your system -s, --single Use a single Markdown file instead of a book configuration file -n, --no-fancy Disably fancy UI -v, --verbose Print warnings in parsing/rendering -a, --autograph Prompts for an autograph for this book -q, --quiet Don't print info/error messages -c, --create ... Create a new book with existing Markdown files -o, --output Specify output file -t, --to Generate specific format --set ... Set a list of book options -l, --list-options List all possible options -L, --lang Set the runtime language used by Crowbook --print-template Prints the default content of a template -S, --stats Print some project statistics -h, --help Print help -V, --version Print version ARGS: [BOOK] File containing the book configuration file, or a Markdown file when called with --single ``` Notes: - Typo in help: `Disably fancy UI` (sic). - Two spaces after the description line (`Render ... HTML.\n \nUSAGE:` — a line containing two spaces). - `-h` is identical to `--help`. Both exit 0. ## 2. `--version` / `-V` STDOUT (stderr empty), exit 0: ``` crowbook 0.17.0 ``` `-V` identical. ## 3. No arguments `crowbook` → exit **0** (not an error exit!), STDOUT empty, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` (there is a trailing blank line after `--help.`) - Same with `-n`/`--no-fancy` and with `-v`: identical bytes. - With `-q` (quiet): the `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` header disappears, but the ERROR text is STILL printed (quiet does not silence this error): ``` ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` - With `--force-emoji` (fancy): STDERR: ``` 🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0 💣 ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` - With `--force-emoji -n`: header keeps emoji, message loses the bomb: ``` 🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0 ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` - This error line has NO brackets (`ERROR msg`, never `[ERROR] msg`), in all modes. ## 4. clap-style argument errors (exit code 2, all on STDERR, STDOUT empty) Unknown long flag `crowbook --nonsense`: ``` error: unexpected argument '--nonsense' found tip: to pass '--nonsense' as a value, use '-- --nonsense' Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Unknown short flag `crowbook -z`: ``` error: unexpected argument '-z' found tip: to pass '-z' as a value, use '-- -z' Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook --to`: ``` error: a value is required for '--to ' but none was supplied [possible values: epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook -o`: ``` error: a value is required for '--output ' but none was supplied For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook -L`: ``` error: a value is required for '--lang ' but none was supplied For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook --print-template`: ``` error: a value is required for '--print-template ' but none was supplied For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook --create`: ``` error: a value is required for '--create ...' but none was supplied For more information, try '--help'. ``` Missing value `crowbook --set`: ``` error: a value is required for '--set ...' but none was supplied For more information, try '--help'. ``` Invalid `--to` value `crowbook --to foo book.book` (also `--to HTML`, case-sensitive): ``` error: invalid value 'foo' for '--to ' [possible values: epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Valid values (clap list): `epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir`. BUT see §7: `odt` is accepted by clap yet rejected at runtime (`ERROR unknown format odt`). Duplicate flag `crowbook --to html --to epub book.book`: ``` error: the argument '--to ' cannot be used multiple times Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Same message shape for `-o a -o b` (`'--output '`) and `-s -s` (`'--single'`). Conflicting flags `crowbook -q -v`: ``` error: the argument '--quiet' cannot be used with '--verbose' Usage: executable --quiet [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` (Note the specialized Usage line.) Same for `-v -q`. Extra positional `crowbook book.book extra.book`: ``` error: unexpected argument 'extra.book' found Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` `--` separator works: `crowbook -- --nonsense` treats `--nonsense` as BOOK: exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Could not find file '--nonsense' for book ``` Combined short flags work: `crowbook -sq book.book` → exit 0, completely silent. ## 5. `--set` parsing `--set ...` is a greedy variadic option: if BOOK is given AFTER `--set`, it is swallowed as a `--set` value. E.g. `crowbook --set foo bar book.book` → exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help. ``` So BOOK must come first: `crowbook book.book --set key value ...`. Only 1 value `crowbook book.book --set title` → clap error, exit 2: ``` error: 2 values required by '--set ...'; only 1 was provided Usage: executable [OPTIONS] [BOOK] For more information, try '--help'. ``` Same for `--set title=X` (the `=` form is NOT split into key/value; counts as 1 value). Odd number of values `crowbook book.book --set a b c` → exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR An odd number of arguments was passed to --set, but it takes a list of key value pairs. ``` (note the line break after `takes`, and trailing blank line; trailing period present) Unknown key `crowbook book.book --set foo bar` → exit 0: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Error in setting key foo: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'foo' ``` (`book.book:4` = the line in the config file after the last parsed line, i.e. where the virtual option line would have been.) Unknown dotted key `book.book --set unknown.key val`: ``` ERROR Error in setting key unknown.key: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: unrecognized key 'unknown.key' ``` Invalid boolean `book.book --set rendering.initials maybe` → exit 0: ``` ERROR Error in setting key rendering.initials: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: expected a boolean as value for key 'rendering.initials', found String("maybe") ``` (`rendering.initials true` works.) Invalid integer `book.book --set epub.version abc` → exit 0: ``` ERROR Error in setting key epub.version: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: expected an integer as value for key 'epub.version', found String("abc") ``` Empty value `book.book --set title ""` → exit 0: ``` ERROR Error in setting key title: book.book:4: Error converting BookOption: value '' for key 'title' does not contain one and only one YAML value ``` Valid override `book.book --set title "Set Title" -t html -o -` → renders with `Set Title`; exit 0. Multiple pairs in one `--set` work: `book.book --set rendering.initials true title Foo -t html -o set4.html` applied both (`Foo`). Values are YAML-parsed (error messages mention YAML; `String("maybe")` Debug format). ## 6. `--lang` / `-L` - Sets the runtime UI language, independent of the book's `lang:` metadata. - `-L fr` with a missing book translates the error: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Impossible de trouver le fichier 'missing.book' pour book ``` (note: `pour book` — the word "book" is NOT translated). - But the no-BOOK error is NOT translated even with `-L fr` (printed before the language is applied): ``` ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. ``` - Unknown language `-L xx`: silently falls back to English, exit 0. - The success/info messages are NOT translated: `-L fr -n -t html -o fr.html book.book`: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): fr.html ``` - `-L fr -l` (list-options): still entirely in English. ## 7. `--to` / `-t` and `--output` / `-o` - Valid clap values: `epub, pdf, html, tex, odt, html.dir` (case-sensitive). - `-t html` with no `output.html` in the book and no `-o`: renders the full standalone HTML to STDOUT (stderr only has `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`). Exit 0. - `-t html -o -`: explicitly renders to STDOUT. Same result. Exit 0. - `-t epub` with no output configured: writes the binary EPUB (zip, starts with `PK`) to STDOUT. Also `-t epub -o -`. STDERR additionally shows the zip warning (see §12). Exit 0. - `-t tex -o -`: renders the LaTeX source to STDOUT. Exit 0. - `-t pdf` (any `-o`): fails because no LaTeX is installed. Exit **0**. STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex' ``` (trailing blank line) - `-t odt -o -` (also with a real file): clap accepts `odt` but the renderer does not. Exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR unknown format odt ``` - `-t html.dir -o hdir book.book` (no `output.html.dir` option set): **PANIC**, exit **101**. An empty directory `hdir` is created. With no `--to` and no output options: renders nothing, exit 0, stderr just `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. - `-s -t html ch1.md` → standalone HTML on stdout (empty `<title>`, empty author meta). Exit 0. - `-s -t html -o single.html ch1.md` → writes file, silent, exit 0. - `-s -` reads Markdown from STDIN: `echo '# Hi' | crowbook -s -t html -o - -` emits HTML on stdout; `... -o out_dash.html -` writes the file. Exit 0. - `-s nonexistent.md` → exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR nonexistent.md: Could not find file 'nonexistent.md' for book chapter ``` - `-s` with a directory as argument: `crowbook -s -t html -o d2.html /tmp`: ``` ERROR /tmp: Error parsing markdown: file tmp contains invalid UTF-8 ``` ## 9. Missing / invalid input files (all exit 0!) Missing book `crowbook nonexistent.book`: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Could not find file 'nonexistent.book' for book ``` Missing chapter (config line `+ missing.md` at line 4): ``` ERROR p4.book:4: Could not find file 'missing.md' for book chapter ``` Chapter file name containing whitespace (`- Appendix Stuff` at line 6) leaks an untranslated l10n key: ``` ERROR parts.book:6: Error parsing configuration file: error.chapter_whitespace ``` Invalid part definition (`@Part One` without a space after `@`; `@ Part One` with a space is valid): ``` ERROR p6.book:4: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid part definition in the chapter list ``` Invalid UTF-8 in a chapter file: ``` ERROR badutf8.book:4: Error parsing markdown: file bad.md contains invalid UTF-8 ``` BOOK argument is a directory (`crowbook -t html -o d.html /tmp`): ``` ERROR Error parsing configuration file: could not read source: Is a directory (os error 21) ``` Markdown "bad syntax" per se is not an error (lenient parser); only I/O and UTF-8 problems are. ## 10. `--create` / `-c` - `--create` with no files: clap error, exit 2 (see §4). - `crowbook --create a1.md a2.md`: does NOT create any file, does NOT prompt (even when stdin/stdout are a pty — verified with `script(1)`). Verified byte-level: `Enter autograph:\n`. - The entered text is injected into the output as `
\n To my dear reader\n
` (HTML). - With EOF on stdin (`< /dev/null`): proceeds with empty autograph, no error. - Same prompt in fancy and `-n` mode. Exit 0 throughout. ## 12. Message formats: fancy (default) vs `--no-fancy` vs `--verbose` vs `--quiet` Banner: every non-quiet run that gets past clap prints `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` as the first STDERR line. `--quiet` removes the banner. With `--force-emoji` the banner becomes `🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0`. ### Default (fancy), piped - On success (e.g. `-t html -o f.html`): STDERR is ONLY `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. Success messages are NOT shown. - Non-fatal warnings are aggregated at the END (rendering `out.book` with `output.html` + `output.epub`, where no `zip` binary exists): ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: WARNING Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library ``` (bare `WARNING` word, no brackets; trailing blank line) - With `--force-emoji` the same becomes: ``` 🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0 ⚠️ WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: ⚠️ WARNING Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library ``` - Fatal errors: `ERROR ` (bare word; with `--force-emoji`: `💣 ERROR `). - On a real tty (tested via `script(1)`), fancy mode draws an animated spinner/progress UI on stderr using `\r` and `ESC[2K`, e.g. `- setting options`, `\ Parsing chapters`, a line of `─` (U+2500), and finishes with lines like `V Finished` and `V html: generated pty2.html`. When piped, all of this is suppressed. ### `--no-fancy` / `-n` Uses a log-like format with brackets, printed as events happen: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [WARN] Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library [INFO] Succesfully generated EPUB: ../../../dev/null ``` ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): fr.html ``` Notes: - Typo in all success messages: `Succesfully` (missing `s`). - Per-format success strings observed: `Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): ` and `Succesfully generated EPUB: `. - The final top-level ERROR is still printed WITHOUT brackets even in `-n` mode, e.g. `-n -t html -o nodir/x.html`: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR could not create file 'nodir/x.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` ### `--verbose` / `-v` env_logger-style lines with `HH:MM:SS`, level, thread id and module path: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Ignoring YAML block: 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Attempting to generate epub... 08:14:10 [WARN] crowbook::epub: Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (3) epub_builder::toc: rendered elem: "
  • 1. Chapter One
    • " 08:14:10 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): rendered.html 08:14:10 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated EPUB: rendered.epub ``` Final ERROR stays bracket-less: `ERROR could not create file ...`. `-v -n` behaves the same as `-v` (no conflict). `-v -q` is a clap conflict (exit 2, see §4). ### `--quiet` / `-q` - Successful run: completely silent (no banner, nothing), exit 0. - Errors are STILL printed (without banner, without brackets): ``` ERROR could not create file 'nodir/x.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` So `--quiet` does not actually suppress error messages despite its help text (`Don't print info/error messages`); it suppresses the banner, info and warnings. ### Brackets vs no brackets — summary - `[WARN]`/`[INFO]`/`[DEBUG]` (and logger `[ERROR]` in `-v`): only from the `-n` plain logger or the `-v` env_logger. - Bare `ERROR msg`: the top-level error printer, used in EVERY mode (fancy, no-fancy, quiet, verbose). No trailing period on most ERROR lines; exceptions with trailing periods: `... book configuration file.`, `For more information try --help.`, `... a list of key value pairs.`. - Bare `WARNING msg` (aggregated) only in fancy mode. - All diagnostics go to STDERR; only render output, `--stats`, `--create`, `--list-options`, `--print-template`, `--help`, `--version` and the `Enter autograph:` prompt go to STDOUT. ## 13. `--stats` / `-S` `crowbook -S book.book` → exit 0, STDOUT (stderr: banner): ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- ch1.md 50 9 5.56 ch2.md 42 7 6.00 --------- TOTAL: 92 16 5.75 ``` - Column layout: left-aligned chapter filename padded to the longest file name, then three right-aligned numeric fields of widths 12, 11, 12. Header words `Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word` align to the same fields. - The separator line is ALWAYS exactly `---------` (9 dashes), regardless of table width. - Numbers: integers for Chars/Words; `Chars/Word` with 2 decimals. - A blank line is printed after the TOTAL row. - With a part (`@ Part One`), the part title gets its own row with an EMPTY chapter name counting the words of the part title itself: ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- 8 2 4.00 ch1.md 50 9 5.56 --------- TOTAL: 58 11 5.27 ``` - Long file names widen the table (37-char name → every line 72 chars wide): ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- 8 2 4.00 a_very_long_chapter_name_for_stats.md 50 9 5.56 ch2.md 42 7 6.00 --------- TOTAL: 100 18 5.56 ``` - `-S -s ch1.md` works (single file = one row). - `-S -q book.book`: table still printed, no banner. - No pluralization anywhere (it is a fixed table, no `word(s)` strings). - EMPTY book (config with no chapters): **PANIC**, exit **101**: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 thread 'main' (2764) panicked at src/lib/stats.rs:285:14: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace ``` (STDOUT empty.) ## 14. `--list-options` / `-l` Exit 0, all on STDOUT (326 lines). Grouped sections with headers: `METADATA`, `ADDITIONAL METADATA`, `OUTPUT OPTIONS`, `RENDERING OPTIONS`, `SPECIAL OPTIONS`, `HTML OPTIONS`, `STANDALONE HTML OPTIONS`, `MULTIFILE HTML OPTIONS`, `EPUB OPTIONS`, `LATEX OPTIONS`, `RESOURCES OPTIONS`, `INPUT OPTIONS #[SERDE(FLATTEN)]` (sic — the serde attribute leaks into the header), `CROWBOOK OPTIONS`. Each entry format: ``` rendering.initials type: boolean (default: false) Use initials ('lettrines') for first letter of a chapter ``` Types seen: `metadata`, `path`, `string`, `boolean`, `integer`, `list of strings`, `template path`. Defaults shown as `(default: ...)`, `not set`, or `""`. Not translated by `-L fr`. Full copy captured in the scratch file `listopt.txt`; first lines: ``` METADATA author type: metadata (default: "") Author of the book title type: metadata (default: "") Title of the book lang type: metadata (default: en) Language of the book ``` Notable defaults: `epub.version` integer default 2; `tex.command` default `xelatex`; `crowbook.zip.command` default `zip`; `tex.class` default `book`; `tex.paper.size` default `a5paper`. ## 15. `--print-template` - Missing value: clap error, exit 2 (§4). - Valid names confirmed: `html.css`, `epub.css`, `tex.template`, `html.standalone.js` (prints the default content to STDOUT, exit 0, banner on stderr). - Any other name, e.g. `crowbook --print-template foo` → exit 0, STDOUT empty: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR foo is not a valid template name ``` Same for `html`, `epub`, `tex`, `html.html`, `epub.html`, `html_dir`, `html.dir.template`, `html_dir.html`, `html_dir.css`, `html.toc`, `html.index`, `epub.toc.ncx`, `epub.titlepage`, `epub.titlepage.xhtml`, `epub.chapter.xhtml`, `html.highlight.css`, `html.highlight.js`, `html.css.print`, `html.css.colors`, `html.js`, `proofread.html`, `tex.template.add` — all rejected. ## 16. Exit codes — summary | Situation | Exit code | |---|---| | success (render, stats, list-options, print-template, create, help, version) | 0 | | no BOOK argument (`ERROR You must pass...`) | 0 | | missing book file / missing chapter file | 0 | | invalid config syntax, invalid UTF-8 chapter | 0 | | invalid `--to` value at runtime (`odt`), render failure (xelatex missing, output file not creatable) | 0 | | unknown/invalid `--set` key or value, odd `--set` count | 0 | | invalid `--print-template` name | 0 | | all clap usage errors (unknown flag, missing value, duplicate/conflicting flags, extra positional) | 2 | | panics: `--stats` on chapter-less book; `-t html.dir` without `output.html.dir` option | 101 | i.e. almost every application-level error still exits 0; only argument-parse errors (2) and Rust panics (101) use non-zero codes. Panic messages include the source path (`src/lib/stats.rs:285:14`, `src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64`) and the line `note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace`. ## 17. Misc - `--force-emoji` only affects the banner and the fancy `ERROR`/`WARNING` prefixes (see §3, §12). It never fails even piped. - `-f` is the short form of `--force-emoji`. - `crowbook -s book.book` (feeding a config file as markdown): parses fine as markdown, renders nothing without `--to`/outputs, exit 0, silent. - BOOK given before `--set` is required; BOOK after `--set` is swallowed (§5). - The aggregated fancy warning footer reads exactly `WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:` (warnings are called "errors" in that line). With no `--to` and no output options: renders nothing, exit 0, stderr just `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. - `-s -t html ch1.md` → standalone HTML on stdout (empty `<title>`, empty author meta). Exit 0. - `-s -t html -o single.html ch1.md` → writes file, silent, exit 0. - `-s -` reads Markdown from STDIN: `echo '# Hi' | crowbook -s -t html -o - -` emits HTML on stdout; `... -o out_dash.html -` writes the file. Exit 0. - `-s nonexistent.md` → exit 0, STDERR: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR nonexistent.md: Could not find file 'nonexistent.md' for book chapter ``` - `-s` with a directory as argument: `crowbook -s -t html -o d2.html /tmp`: ``` ERROR /tmp: Error parsing markdown: file tmp contains invalid UTF-8 ``` ## 9. Missing / invalid input files (all exit 0!) Missing book `crowbook nonexistent.book`: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Could not find file 'nonexistent.book' for book ``` Missing chapter (config line `+ missing.md` at line 4): ``` ERROR p4.book:4: Could not find file 'missing.md' for book chapter ``` Chapter file name containing whitespace (`- Appendix Stuff` at line 6) leaks an untranslated l10n key: ``` ERROR parts.book:6: Error parsing configuration file: error.chapter_whitespace ``` Invalid part definition (`@Part One` without a space after `@`; `@ Part One` with a space is valid): ``` ERROR p6.book:4: Error parsing configuration file: found invalid part definition in the chapter list ``` Invalid UTF-8 in a chapter file: ``` ERROR badutf8.book:4: Error parsing markdown: file bad.md contains invalid UTF-8 ``` BOOK argument is a directory (`crowbook -t html -o d.html /tmp`): ``` ERROR Error parsing configuration file: could not read source: Is a directory (os error 21) ``` Markdown "bad syntax" per se is not an error (lenient parser); only I/O and UTF-8 problems are. ## 10. `--create` / `-c` - `--create` with no files: clap error, exit 2 (see §4). - `crowbook --create a1.md a2.md`: does NOT create any file, does NOT prompt (even when stdin/stdout are a pty — verified with `script(1)`). It prints the generated book configuration to STDOUT and exits 0. Files listed are NOT checked for existence (works with `nope1.md nope2.md` too). - STDOUT verbatim (note: the option lines are surrounded by double quotes — they are printed via a Debug-style formatter — while the chapter-list lines are not): ``` "author: Your name" "title: Your title" "lang: en" "## Output formats" "# Uncomment and fill to generate files" "# output.html: some_file.html" "# output.epub: some_file.epub" "# output.pdf: some_file.pdf" "# Or uncomment the following to generate PDF, HTML and EPUB files based on this file's name" "# output: [pdf, epub, html]" "# Uncomment and fill to set cover image (for EPUB)" "# cover: some_cover.png" ## List of chapters + a1.md + a2.md ``` - STDERR: just `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. `-n` does not change the output. ## 11. `--autograph` / `-a` - Prints the prompt `Enter autograph:` (WITH trailing `\n`) to STDOUT, then reads one line from stdin. Verified byte-level: `Enter autograph:\n`. - The entered text is injected into the output as `
\n To my dear reader\n
` (HTML). - With EOF on stdin (`< /dev/null`): proceeds with empty autograph, no error. - Same prompt in fancy and `-n` mode. Exit 0 throughout. ## 12. Message formats: fancy (default) vs `--no-fancy` vs `--verbose` vs `--quiet` Banner: every non-quiet run that gets past clap prints `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` as the first STDERR line. `--quiet` removes the banner. With `--force-emoji` the banner becomes `🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0`. ### Default (fancy), piped - On success (e.g. `-t html -o f.html`): STDERR is ONLY `CROWBOOK 0.17.0`. Success messages are NOT shown. - Non-fatal warnings are aggregated at the END (rendering `out.book` with `output.html` + `output.epub`, where no `zip` binary exists): ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: WARNING Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library ``` (bare `WARNING` word, no brackets; trailing blank line) - With `--force-emoji` the same becomes: ``` 🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0 ⚠️ WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred: ⚠️ WARNING Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library ``` - Fatal errors: `ERROR ` (bare word; with `--force-emoji`: `💣 ERROR `). - On a real tty (tested via `script(1)`), fancy mode draws an animated spinner/progress UI on stderr using `\r` and `ESC[2K`, e.g. `- setting options`, `\ Parsing chapters`, a line of `─` (U+2500), and finishes with lines like `V Finished` and `V html: generated pty2.html`. When piped, all of this is suppressed. ### `--no-fancy` / `-n` Uses a log-like format with brackets, printed as events happen: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [WARN] Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library [INFO] Succesfully generated EPUB: ../../../dev/null ``` ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): fr.html ``` Notes: - Typo in all success messages: `Succesfully` (missing `s`). - Per-format success strings observed: `Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): ` and `Succesfully generated EPUB: `. - The final top-level ERROR is still printed WITHOUT brackets even in `-n` mode, e.g. `-n -t html -o nodir/x.html`: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR could not create file 'nodir/x.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` ### `--verbose` / `-v` env_logger-style lines with `HH:MM:SS`, level, thread id and module path: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Ignoring YAML block: 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: Attempting to generate epub... 08:14:10 [WARN] crowbook::epub: Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library 08:14:10 [DEBUG] (3) epub_builder::toc: rendered elem: "
  • 1. Chapter One
    • " 08:14:10 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): rendered.html 08:14:10 [INFO] crowbook::book: Succesfully generated EPUB: rendered.epub ``` Final ERROR stays bracket-less: `ERROR could not create file ...`. `-v -n` behaves the same as `-v` (no conflict). `-v -q` is a clap conflict (exit 2, see §4). ### `--quiet` / `-q` - Successful run: completely silent (no banner, nothing), exit 0. - Errors are STILL printed (without banner, without brackets): ``` ERROR could not create file 'nodir/x.html': 'No such file or directory (os error 2) ``` So `--quiet` does not actually suppress error messages despite its help text (`Don't print info/error messages`); it suppresses the banner, info and warnings. ### Brackets vs no brackets — summary - `[WARN]`/`[INFO]`/`[DEBUG]` (and logger `[ERROR]` in `-v`): only from the `-n` plain logger or the `-v` env_logger. - Bare `ERROR msg`: the top-level error printer, used in EVERY mode (fancy, no-fancy, quiet, verbose). No trailing period on most ERROR lines; exceptions with trailing periods: `... book configuration file.`, `For more information try --help.`, `... a list of key value pairs.`. - Bare `WARNING msg` (aggregated) only in fancy mode. - All diagnostics go to STDERR; only render output, `--stats`, `--create`, `--list-options`, `--print-template`, `--help`, `--version` and the `Enter autograph:` prompt go to STDOUT. ## 13. `--stats` / `-S` `crowbook -S book.book` → exit 0, STDOUT (stderr: banner): ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- ch1.md 50 9 5.56 ch2.md 42 7 6.00 --------- TOTAL: 92 16 5.75 ``` - Column layout: left-aligned chapter filename padded to the longest file name, then three right-aligned numeric fields of widths 12, 11, 12. Header words `Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word` align to the same fields. - The separator line is ALWAYS exactly `---------` (9 dashes), regardless of table width. - Numbers: integers for Chars/Words; `Chars/Word` with 2 decimals. - A blank line is printed after the TOTAL row. - With a part (`@ Part One`), the part title gets its own row with an EMPTY chapter name counting the words of the part title itself: ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- 8 2 4.00 ch1.md 50 9 5.56 --------- TOTAL: 58 11 5.27 ``` - Long file names widen the table (37-char name → every line 72 chars wide): ``` Chapter Chars Words Chars/Word --------- 8 2 4.00 a_very_long_chapter_name_for_stats.md 50 9 5.56 ch2.md 42 7 6.00 --------- TOTAL: 100 18 5.56 ``` - `-S -s ch1.md` works (single file = one row). - `-S -q book.book`: table still printed, no banner. - No pluralization anywhere (it is a fixed table, no `word(s)` strings). - EMPTY book (config with no chapters): **PANIC**, exit **101**: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 thread 'main' (2764) panicked at src/lib/stats.rs:285:14: called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace ``` (STDOUT empty.) ## 14. `--list-options` / `-l` Exit 0, all on STDOUT (326 lines). Grouped sections with headers: `METADATA`, `ADDITIONAL METADATA`, `OUTPUT OPTIONS`, `RENDERING OPTIONS`, `SPECIAL OPTIONS`, `HTML OPTIONS`, `STANDALONE HTML OPTIONS`, `MULTIFILE HTML OPTIONS`, `EPUB OPTIONS`, `LATEX OPTIONS`, `RESOURCES OPTIONS`, `INPUT OPTIONS #[SERDE(FLATTEN)]` (sic — the serde attribute leaks into the header), `CROWBOOK OPTIONS`. Each entry format: ``` rendering.initials type: boolean (default: false) Use initials ('lettrines') for first letter of a chapter ``` Types seen: `metadata`, `path`, `string`, `boolean`, `integer`, `list of strings`, `template path`. Defaults shown as `(default: ...)`, `not set`, or `""`. Not translated by `-L fr`. Full copy captured in the scratch file `listopt.txt`; first lines: ``` METADATA author type: metadata (default: "") Author of the book title type: metadata (default: "") Title of the book lang type: metadata (default: en) Language of the book ``` Notable defaults: `epub.version` integer default 2; `tex.command` default `xelatex`; `crowbook.zip.command` default `zip`; `tex.class` default `book`; `tex.paper.size` default `a5paper`. ## 15. `--print-template` - Missing value: clap error, exit 2 (§4). - Valid names confirmed: `html.css`, `epub.css`, `tex.template`, `html.standalone.js` (prints the default content to STDOUT, exit 0, banner on stderr). - Any other name, e.g. `crowbook --print-template foo` → exit 0, STDOUT empty: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR foo is not a valid template name ``` Same for `html`, `epub`, `tex`, `html.html`, `epub.html`, `html_dir`, `html.dir.template`, `html_dir.html`, `html_dir.css`, `html.toc`, `html.index`, `epub.toc.ncx`, `epub.titlepage`, `epub.titlepage.xhtml`, `epub.chapter.xhtml`, `html.highlight.css`, `html.highlight.js`, `html.css.print`, `html.css.colors`, `html.js`, `proofread.html`, `tex.template.add` — all rejected. ## 16. Exit codes — summary | Situation | Exit code | |---|---| | success (render, stats, list-options, print-template, create, help, version) | 0 | | no BOOK argument (`ERROR You must pass...`) | 0 | | missing book file / missing chapter file | 0 | | invalid config syntax, invalid UTF-8 chapter | 0 | | invalid `--to` value at runtime (`odt`), render failure (xelatex missing, output file not creatable) | 0 | | unknown/invalid `--set` key or value, odd `--set` count | 0 | | invalid `--print-template` name | 0 | | all clap usage errors (unknown flag, missing value, duplicate/conflicting flags, extra positional) | 2 | | panics: `--stats` on chapter-less book; `-t html.dir` without `output.html.dir` option | 101 | i.e. almost every application-level error still exits 0; only argument-parse errors (2) and Rust panics (101) use non-zero codes. Panic messages include the source path (`src/lib/stats.rs:285:14`, `src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64`) and the line `note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace`. ## 17. Misc - `--force-emoji` only affects the banner and the fancy `ERROR`/`WARNING` prefixes (see §3, §12). It never fails even piped. - `-f` is the short form of `--force-emoji`. - `crowbook -s book.book` (feeding a config file as markdown): parses fine as markdown, renders nothing without `--to`/outputs, exit 0, silent. - BOOK given before `--set` is required; BOOK after `--set` is swallowed (§5). - The aggregated fancy warning footer reads exactly `WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:` (warnings are called "errors" in that line). payload.resultSummary:
Report written to `/workspace/ref/reports/cli.md` (~730 lines, fully verbatim outputs with stdout/stderr separated and exit codes).

## Key findings

**Exit codes are broken by convention**: nearly every application-level error (missing book, missing chapter, render failure, invalid `--set`, invalid template name, unknown runtime format) exits **0**. Only clap argument errors exit **2**, and two panics exit **101** (`--stats` on a chapter-less book → `src/lib/stats.rs:285` unwrap; `-t html.dir` without `output.html.dir` option → `src/lib/html_dir.rs:464` unwrap, after creating an empty output dir).

**`--set` is a greedy variadic**: BOOK placed after `--set` gets swallowed as a value (yields the "You must pass the name of a book configuration file." error). Odd counts give a two-line error with trailing blank line; unknown keys/invalid bool/int values produce `Error converting BookOption: ...` messages with YAML Debug formatting like `String("maybe")`.

**Message format rules**:
- Banner `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` on stderr in all non-quiet runs; `--force-emoji` makes it `🐦 CROWBOOK 📚 0.17.0`.
- Default fancy mode (piped): hides success messages entirely; aggregates warnings at end as bare `WARNING ...` lines headed by `WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:`.
- `-n`: bracketed `[WARN]`/`[INFO]` logger lines; `-v`: timestamped env_logger format (`08:14:10 [DEBUG] (1) crowbook::book: ...`).
- The top-level error printer is always bare `ERROR msg` (no brackets) in every mode, including `-n` and `-q`. `-q` does NOT suppress errors despite its help text — only banner/info/warnings.
- Typos preserved: `Disably fancy UI` (help), `Succesfully generated ...` (all success messages), unbalanced quote in `could not create file 'x': 'No such file or directory (os error 2)`.

**Notable behaviors**: `--create` never creates files or prompts — it prints the generated config to stdout with option lines wrapped in double quotes; `--autograph` prompts `Enter autograph:` on stdout and reads one stdin line; `-s -` reads Markdown from stdin; `-t odt` is accepted by clap but fails at runtime (`ERROR unknown format odt`); `-t epub` with no output configured dumps binary zip to stdout; `--stats` separator is always exactly 9 dashes, part titles produce rows with empty chapter names, no pluralization exists; `-L fr` translates only some errors (`Impossible de trouver le fichier 'x' pour book` — "book" untranslated) but not the no-args error or success messages.

## 8. Smart quotes (input.clean.smart_quotes, default true) — English

Input `smart.md`:

```
"He said 'hello' to me." It's John's book. 'Twas the night.

"double at start" and end "like this" and "unbalanced.

Apostrophes: don't, can't, 'tis.
```

Output (default):

```html

        “He said ‘hello’ to me.” It’s John’s book. ’Twas the night.
        

        “double at start” and end “like this” and “unbalanced.
        

        Apostrophes: don’t, can’t, ’tis.
        
```

- Straight quotes become U+201C/U+201D (“ ”) and U+2018/U+2019 (‘ ’); apostrophes -> U+2019.
- Leading `'Twas` becomes `’Twas` (apostrophe, correct).
- An unbalanced `"` at end becomes an OPENING quote `“unbalanced.`
  (opening is the fallback guess).
- `--set input.clean.smart_quotes false` leaves all quotes vertical.
- `--set input.clean false` disables smart quotes AND collapses of multiple spaces:
  with clean on, `"a"   b` -> `“a” b` (multiple spaces collapsed to one);
  with clean off the runs of spaces are preserved verbatim.

## 9. French typography cleaning (--set lang fr)

Input `french.md`:

```
Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.

« Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d'espace».

Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?

2 % et 10 € environ.
```

Default output (html.escape_nb_spaces true) — verbatim:

```html

        Chapitre 1
        Typographie
        Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.
        

        « Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d’espace».
        

        Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?
        

        2 % et 10 € environ.
        
```

`--set lang fr html.escape_nb_spaces false` output (verbatim text), byte-checked with `od -c`:

```html

        Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.
        

        « Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d’espace».
        

        Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?
        

        2 % et 10 € environ.
        
```

Byte-level findings (od output, 342 200 257 = U+202F narrow no-break space,
302 240 = U+00A0 no-break space):

- Existing space before `!`, `?`, `;`, `%`, `€` and INSIDE `« »` -> **U+202F** (narrow
  no-break space). Existing space before `:` -> **U+00A0** (plain no-break space).
- The cleaner NEVER inserts a space that wasn't there: `Bonjour!` stays `Bonjour!`,
  `«pas d'espace»` stays without inner spaces (input `«pas d'espace»` -> `«pas d’espace»`).
- Guillemet edge case (minimal tests, fr2.md): a `« ... »` pair at the START of a paragraph
  keeps U+00A0 inside (`«\u00A0abc\u00A0»`), but mid-sentence pairs get U+202F
  (`x «\u202Fabc\u202F» y`). With inner punctuation: paragraph-start `« abc ! »` ->
  `«\u00A0abc\u202F!\u00A0»`.
- `html.escape_nb_spaces true` (default): every U+202F is rendered as
  ` `-style markup — actually the span wraps the
  PRECEDING word plus the punctuation: `Bonjour !`;
  for guillemets the whole `« ... »` group: `« Bonjour ! »`.
  U+00A0 (before `:` and at-paragraph-start guillemets) is left as a literal U+00A0 char
  (raw byte 302 240, no span, no entity).
- French also converts `...` to the single char `…` (U+2026) — English does NOT (English
  leaves `...` unchanged). Spaces inside `. . .` become U+00A0 (`. . .`).
- French adds U+00A0 adjacent to dashes (see §10): `A – dash — and` (after `--`/`---`
  ligature) became `A –\u00A0dash\u00A0— and`, `—-\u00A0four`.
- `lang: fr` also localizes the chapter header ("Chapitre 1"), the ``,
  and the inline TOC default title ("Table des matières").
- `lang` may be set via the top-of-file YAML metadata block with the same effect
  (tested: `lang: fr` in YAML produced `Bonjour !`).

## 10. Ligature options (default: both false)

Input `lig.md`:

```
A -- dash --- and ---- four.

<< guillemets >> and <>.

Ellipsis... and . . . dots.
```

- Default (English): unchanged; `<<`/`>>` are escaped as text: `<< guillemets >>`.
- `--set input.clean.ligature.dashes true`:
  `A – dash — and —- four.` — `--`->U+2013 (–), `---`->U+2014 (—), `----`->`—-`
  (greedy: em dash consumes 3, leftover `-`). Applied to `<<...`? no.
- `--set input.clean.ligature.guillemets true`:
  `« guillemets » and «unspaced».` — `<<`->`«`, `>>`->`»`; existing inner spaces are kept
  as-is (regular spaces in English).
- Both + `lang fr`: ligatures applied, THEN French spacing applies to real `« »` but the
  ligature-produced guillemets at paragraph start got U+00A0 (`«\u00A0guillemets\u00A0»`),
  consistent with §9; `...` -> `…`; dashes got adjacent U+00A0s.
- `(c) (r) (tm)` are never touched.

## 11. Superscript/subscript (crowbook.markdown.superscript, default false)

Input `sup.md`:

```
E = mc^2^ and H~2~O and x^2 + y^2^ mixed.
```

- Default: `^` left literal, but `~2~` is parsed as STRIKETHROUGH:
  `E = mc^2^ and H2O and x^2 + y^2^ mixed.`
- With `--set crowbook.markdown.superscript true`:
  `E = mc2 and H2O and x2 + y2^ mixed.`
  (`^...^` -> ``, `~...~` -> ``; spans can contain spaces; `x^2 + y^2^` pairs the
  first `^` with the NEXT `^`, i.e. `2 + y` then literal `2^`.)
- Unclosed `A^not closed` / `~also not` stay literal in both modes.

## 12. rendering.initials and rendering.inline_toc

- `rendering.initials true` adds `class = "first-para"` to the FIRST paragraph of each
  chapter only: `

  A chapter starting with a quote/emphasis still counts if it is a plain paragraph.
- `rendering.inline_toc true` inserts before the chapter div (verbatim, toc.md):

```html
        
        
  
        Table of contents
        
      
          
      
        • 1. Chap A
          • 
      
        • 2. Chap B
          • 
    
        

        
```

  Only level-1 chapters are listed (h2/h3 absent). Entries are numbered `1. ` per
  `rendering.chapter.template` (`{{number}}. {{chapter_title}}`); setting the template to
  `'{{number}}: {{chapter_title}}'` gives `
      1. 1: Chap A
        2. `.
- `rendering.inline_toc.name "Sommaire perso"` -> `
        Sommaire perso
        `.
  Default name is the localized string `{{loc_toc}}`: "Table of contents" (en),
  "Table des matières" (fr with `--set lang fr`).

## 13. HTML blocks / inline HTML, crowbook.html_as_text (default true)

Input `htmlblocks.md`:

```

        
raw html block

        

Para with inline html and 
         tags.





text
```

Default (`html_as_text true`) — everything is escaped to text (and smart-quoted!), verbatim:

```html

        HTML handling
        <div class=“custom”>
raw <b>html</b> block
</div>

        Para with inline <span class=“x”>html</span> and <br> tags.
        
<script>alert(“x”)</script>
<!-- a comment -->

        <unknown-tag foo=“bar”>text</unknown-tag>
        
```

(HTML blocks are emitted as bare escaped text lines, NOT wrapped in `
        `; inline tags are
escaped inside their paragraph.)

`--set crowbook.html_as_text false`:

```html

        HTML handling
        Para with inline html and tags.
        

        text
        
```

HTML BLOCKS ARE DROPPED ENTIRELY (the div block, its content, the script, the comment all
vanish — they are not passed through to the output). Inline tags are stripped but their
text content remains (`html` -> `html`).

## 14. Footnotes

Input `footnotes.md`:

```
Text with a note[^first] and another[^second] and repeat[^first] again.

Also inline note ^[this is inline] here.

[^second]: Second definition with *emph*.

[^first]: First definition
    with continuation line.

Undefined ref[^nope] stays?
```

Output (verbatim):

```html

        Text with a note[first] and another[second] and repeat[first] again.
        

        Also inline note ^[this is inline] here.
        

        Undefined ref[^nope] stays?
        

        
 
        Notes
        

        

        
 
  
        
  [first]

        

         		
 
  
        First definition with continuation line.
        

        
          		

        

        
 
  
        
  [second]

        

         		
 
  
        Second definition with emph.
        

        
          		

        

        

        
```

- Reference: `[NAME]`
  — the footnote's own label is used as the displayed number (`[first]`, `[second]`),
  and as part of the id.
- The numeric prefix is the 1-based index of the source FILE (chapter) in the book: in
  book mode, chapter file 1 -> `note-dest-1-x`, chapter file 2 -> `note-dest-2-y`; in
  single mode everything is file 1.
- A repeated `[^first]` produces a SECOND anchor with the SAME `id = "note-source-1-first"`
  (duplicate id in the document).
- Notes section appended at end of the chapter div: `
        ` (note the
  space before `>`), heading `
        Notes
        `, then a ``
  whose rows pair a backlink cell `[name]`
  with `
        content
        `.
- Ordering follows FIRST REFERENCE order, not definition order (`second` defined first in
  source but listed after `first`).
- Continuation lines in a definition are joined ("First definition with continuation line.").
- Inline notes `^[...]` are NOT supported (left literal). Undefined refs left literal
  (`[^nope]`).

## 9. French typography cleaning (--set lang fr)

Input `french.md`:

```
Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.

« Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d'espace».

Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?

2 % et 10 € environ.
```

Default output (html.escape_nb_spaces true) — verbatim:

```html

        Chapitre 1
        Typographie
        Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.
        

        « Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d’espace».
        

        Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?
        

        2 % et 10 € environ.
        
```

`--set lang fr html.escape_nb_spaces false` output (verbatim text), byte-checked with `od -c`:

```html

        Bonjour ! Comment ça va ? Très bien ; merci : au revoir.
        

        « Guillemets déjà là » et «pas d’espace».
        

        Il dit : « Bonjour ! » Vraiment ?
        

        2 % et 10 € environ.
        
```

Byte-level findings (od output, 342 200 257 = U+202F narrow no-break space,
302 240 = U+00A0 no-break space):

- Existing space before `!`, `?`, `;`, `%`, `€` and INSIDE `« »` -> **U+202F** (narrow
  no-break space). Existing space before `:` -> **U+00A0** (plain no-break space).
- The cleaner NEVER inserts a space that wasn't there: `Bonjour!` stays `Bonjour!`,
  `«pas d'espace»` stays without inner spaces (input `«pas d'espace»` -> `«pas d’espace»`).
- Guillemet edge case (minimal tests, fr2.md): a `« ... »` pair at the START of a paragraph
  keeps U+00A0 inside (`«\u00A0abc\u00A0»`), but mid-sentence pairs get U+202F
  (`x «\u202Fabc\u202F» y`). With inner punctuation: paragraph-start `« abc ! »` ->
  `«\u00A0abc\u202F!\u00A0»`.
- `html.escape_nb_spaces true` (default): every U+202F is rendered as
  ` `-style markup — actually the span wraps the
  PRECEDING word plus the punctuation: `Bonjour !`;
  for guillemets the whole `« ... »` group: `« Bonjour ! »`.
  U+00A0 (before `:` and at-paragraph-start guillemets) is left as a literal U+00A0 char
  (raw byte 302 240, no span, no entity).
- French also converts `...` to the single char `…` (U+2026) — English does NOT (English
  leaves `...` unchanged). Spaces inside `. . .` become U+00A0 (`. . .`).
- French adds U+00A0 adjacent to dashes (see §10): `A – dash — and` (after `--`/`---`
  ligature) became `A –\u00A0dash\u00A0— and`, `—-\u00A0four`.
- `lang: fr` also localizes the chapter header ("Chapitre 1"), the ``,
  and the inline TOC default title ("Table des matières").
- `lang` may be set via the top-of-file YAML metadata block with the same effect
  (tested: `lang: fr` in YAML produced `Bonjour !`).

## 2. tex.class: article vs book

- `--single` mode defaults to **article** (`\documentclass{article}`), even though
  `--list-options` says `tex.class` default is `book`. In book-config mode the class is `book`.
- `--set tex.class book` → `\documentclass{book}`.
- With `book`, the preamble additionally contains a `\renewcommand{\maketitle}{...}` block
  (fancy title page + copyright page, using `<<subtitle>>`, `<<version>>`, `<<license>>`,
  `<<autograph>>`); with any other class that block is absent (only the fancyhdr redefinition).
- Invalid class is passed through verbatim: `--set tex.class nonsense` → `\documentclass{nonsense}`
  (exit 0, no warning; the `book`-only maketitle block is then omitted).

## 3. Headers

Book class (`--set tex.class book`), input with `# H1` … `###### H6`:

```latex
\chapter{H1}
\label{chapter-0}
\section{H2}
\subsection{H3}
\subsubsection{H4}
\paragraoh{H5}
\paragraoh{H6}
```

Article class (default for `--single`), same input:

```latex
\section{H1}
\label{chapter-0}
\section{H2}
\subsection{H3}
\subsubsection{H4}
\paragraoh{H5}
\paragraoh{H6}
```

- **Bug (verbatim): H5 and H6 render as `\paragraoh{...}`** — a typo for `\paragraph` (both levels).
- In article class both H1 and H2 map to `\section` (chapter collapses onto section).
- `\label{chapter-N}` follows the first chapter header; N counts chapters AND parts (see §8).
- If the first header in a `--single` file is H2, it still becomes `\section{...}`.

### rendering.num_depth has NO effect on tex
Outputs for `rendering.num_depth` 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 are byte-identical (verified with `diff`,
both in `--single` and book-config mode). No starred/unstarred switching, no `secnumdepth`.
The only way to get starred commands is an unnumbered chapter (`-` prefix in the .book file):
then the chapter AND all its descendant headers are starred with `\addcontentsline`:

```latex
\section*{Chapter Two}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Chapter Two}
\label{chapter-1}
\section*{Sec}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Sec}
```
(book class: `\chapter*{...}` + `\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{...}`)

## 4. Inline markup

Input:
```
Some *emphasis*, **strong**, ~~strike~~ and `code` text.
```
Output body:
```latex
Some \emph{emphasis}, \mdstrong{strong}, \sout{strike} and \mdcode{code} text.
```
- `\mdstrong` = `\textbf`, `\mdcode` = `\texttt` (defined in preamble).
- Strikethrough uses `\sout`; `\usepackage[normalem]{ulem}` is included only when strike is used.
- `~sub~` also maps to `\sout{...}` (it IS the strikethrough syntax); `^sup^` is NOT supported —
  the carets are escaped: `Super \textasciicircum{}script\textasciicircum{} and sub \sout{script}.`
- Inline code escaping: `` `code $pecial #_chars` `` →
  `\mdcode{code \$pecial \#\_\allowbreak{}chars}` (note `\allowbreak{}` after `\_`).
- `rendering.initials true` → `\usepackage{lettrine}` and first paragraph of chapter starts
  `\lettrine{S}{ome} \emph{emphasis}, ...`.

## 5. Lists, quotes, rule, hardbreak, definition lists, task lists

Input:
```
- item a
- item b

1. one
2. two

> a quote
> second line

---

hard  
break

Term
: definition
```
Output body (verbatim, including missing blank line between environments):
```latex
\begin{itemize}
\item item a


\item item b


\end{itemize}\begin{enumerate}
\item one


\item two



\end{enumerate}
\begin{mdblockquote}
a quote second line


\end{mdblockquote}
\mdrule
hard\mdhardbreak
break

\begin{description}[style=nextline, labelwidth=0pt]
\item[Term]
definition


\end{description}
```
- Block quote joins soft-wrapped lines with a space; uses `mdblockquote` env (`quotation`+`\itshape`).
- `---` → `\mdrule` (centered `***` macro). Hardbreak (two trailing spaces) → `\mdhardbreak` = `\\`.
- Task lists (`- [ ]` / `- [x]`) → itemize items `[$\square$] todo` / `[$\boxtimes$] done`;
  `\usepackage{amssymb}` included only when task items are used.

## 6. Code blocks: syntect vs none

Default (`rendering.highlight: syntect`, theme `InspiredGitHub`): every fenced or indented block
becomes an `mdcodeblock` environment (mdframed) with per-token
`\textcolor[rgb]{r, g, b}{\texttt{...}}`, keywords additionally wrapped in `\textbf{...}`,
spaces as `\hphantom{ }\allowbreak{}`, `(`/`)` get `\allowbreak{}`, line end is `\\{}` and an
extra `\\{}` after the last line. Preamble gains `spverbatim`, `color`, `mdframed` packages and
the `mdcodeblock` env definition (only when the document contains code blocks).

Example (```rust fn main() { println!("hi"); } ```), abridged verbatim start:
```latex
\begin{mdcodeblock}
{\sloppy \textbf{\textcolor[rgb]{0.654902, 0.11372549, 0.3647059}{\texttt{fn}}}\textcolor[rgb]{0.19607843, 0.19607843, 0.19607843}{\texttt{\hphantom{ }\allowbreak{}}}...
\end{mdcodeblock}
```

- No language / unknown language → all tokens in default color `0.19607843, 0.19607843, 0.19607843`.
- Indented code blocks are highlighted too (as plain text).
- `rendering.highlight none` (or any unrecognized value, e.g. `bogus` — silently accepted) →
```latex
\begin{mdcodeblock}
\begin{spverbatim}
fn main() { println!("hi"); }

\end{spverbatim}
\end{mdcodeblock}
```
- Themes: `rendering.highlight.theme 'Solarized (dark)'` and `tex.highlight.theme 'Solarized (dark)'`
  both change the colors (identical results). Invalid theme name: document still renders with the
  default theme, exit 0, stderr:
```
CROWBOOK 0.17.0
WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:
ERROR could not set syntect theme to NoSuchTheme, defaulting to "InspiredGitHub"
```

## 7. Tables, footnotes

Input:
```
| left | center | right | default |
|:-----|:------:|------:|---------|
| a | b | c | d |

Footnote ref[^1] here.

[^1]: footnote text
```
Output:
```latex
\begin{mdtable}{|X|X|X|X|}
\hline
left & center & right & default\\ 
\hline
a & b & c & d\\ 

\hline
\end{mdtable}

Footnote ref\footnotemark[1] here.

\footnotetext[1]{footnote text

}
```
- **Column alignment is ignored**: always `tabularx` with `{|X|X|...|}` (`mdtable` env, preamble
  comment admits: "Crowbook currently always insert \hline at beginning and end of the table").
  Note the literal space after `\\` on row lines.
- Footnotes → `\footnotemark[N]` + deferred `\footnotetext[N]{...}` (with a trailing blank line
  inside the braces).

## 8. Links, images, parts, labels

Input (images must exist or the whole render aborts, see §10):
```
A [link to example](https://example.com) and [relative](page.html#anchor) and autolink <https://foo.bar/baz>.

[ref link][r]

[r]: https://ref.example "title"

An image: ![alt text](img.png) and standalone:

![alone](pic.jpg)
```
Output:
```latex
A \href{https://example.com}{link to example}\protect\footnote{\url{https://example.com}} and \href{page.html\#anchor}{relative}\protect\footnote{\url{page.html\#anchor}} and autolink \url{https://foo.bar/baz}.

\href{https://ref.example}{ref link}\protect\footnote{\url{https://ref.example}}

An image: \mdimage{images/image_0.png} and standalone:

\mdstandaloneimage{images/image_1.jpg}
```
- `tex.links_as_footnotes true` (default) appends `\protect\footnote{\url{...}}` after each
  `\href`; `false` omits it. Autolinks are plain `\url{...}` (never footnoted).
- **Local image files are renamed** in the tex to `images/image_N.<ext>` (N = 0-based order of
  appearance, cover included). `\mdstandaloneimage` = centered `\includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]`,
  `\mdimage` = bare `\includegraphics` (definitions in preamble, only included when images used).
- **Remote images (`https://...`) are silently dropped** — no warning even with `-v`.
- Anchor-only links like `[x](#chapter-1)` are NOT treated as internal:
  `\href{\#chapter-1}{x}\protect\footnote{\url{\#chapter-1}}`.

### Internal links (book config only) and tex.pageref_template
Book with `+ ch1.md` / `+ ch2.md`, link `[chapter two](ch2.md)`:
```latex
Go to \hyperref[chapter-1]{chapter two}\footnote{p\pageref{chapter-1}} and \hyperref[chapter-1]{anchor}\footnote{p\pageref{chapter-1}}.
```
- Default `tex.pageref_template` = `\footnote{p\pageref{<<key>>}}` (note: no `.` after `p`).
- `--set tex.pageref_template 'X<<key>>Y'` → `\hyperref[chapter-1]{chapter two}Xchapter-1Y`.
- `tex.hyperref false` → internal links are NOT resolved; they render as external:
  `\href{ch2.md}{chapter two}\protect\footnote{\url{ch2.md}}`. The `\usepackage{hyperref}` line
  stays in the preamble regardless (option only changes link resolution).

### Parts and chapter counters
Book-config part marker is `@` (line `@ Part One`). Output:
```latex
\setcounter{chapter}{0}\part{Part One}
\label{chapter-0}
\chapter{Chapter One}
\label{chapter-1}
```
- Parts get their own `\label{chapter-N}` (single counter shared with chapters).
- `\setcounter{chapter}{0}` is emitted per part (matches `rendering.part.reset_counter` default true).
- `! Part` is rejected: `ERROR p.book:2: Error parsing configuration file: error.chapter_whitespace`
  (untranslated error key, verbatim).
- `rendering.chapter Chapitre` / `rendering.part Livre` insert after `\begin{document}`:
```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@chapapp}{Chapitre}
\makeatother

\renewcommand{\partname}{Livre}
```
- `rendering.chapter.roman_numerals` / `rendering.part.roman_numerals` /
  `rendering.chapter.template` / `rendering.part.template` produce NO change in the tex output
  (they only affect HTML/EPUB TOC naming; tex TOC is `\tableofcontents`).

## 9. Escaping, smart quotes, French typography, nbsp

Escaping input:
```
Special: # $ % & _ { } ~ ^ \ and < > |.

"quotes" and 'apostrophes' -- dashes --- ellipsis...
```
Output:
```latex
Special: \# \$ \% \& \_ \{ \} \textasciitilde{} \textasciicircum{} \textbackslash{} and \textless{} \textgreater{} |.

“quotes” and ‘apostrophes’ -{}- dashes -{}-{}- ellipsis...
```
- `|` is NOT escaped. `--` → `-{}-`, `---` → `-{}-{}-` (ligature breakers, not dashes).
- Smart quotes (default `input.clean.smart_quotes true`) produce literal UTF-8 curly quotes
  `“ ” ‘ ’`; with `--set input.clean.smart_quotes false` the ASCII quotes pass through.
- Unicode (é, 🎉, € …) passes through raw (preamble assumes xelatex/fontspec).
- Raw inline/block HTML is escaped as text: `<b>` → `\textless{}b\textgreater{}`.
- `input.clean.ligature.dashes true`: `--` → `–`, `---` → `—` (real UTF-8 dashes).
- `input.clean.ligature.guillemets true`: `<<d>>` → `«d»`.

### French (`--set lang fr`), input: `French: « test » nbsp:<NBSP>here nnbsp:<NNBSP>here punct ! ? : ;`
With default `tex.escape_nb_spaces true`:
```latex
French: «\,test\,» nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct\,!{}\,?~:\,;
```
- U+00A0 (nbsp) → `~`, U+202F (narrow nbsp) → `\,`.
- French auto-clean (`input.clean` default true) inserts narrow nbsp before `! ? ;` (→ `\,!{}`,
  `\,?`, `\,;` — note `!` also gains `{}`) and nbsp before `:` (→ `~:`); spaces inside `« »`
  become narrow nbsp (→ `«\,test\,»`).
- With `tex.escape_nb_spaces false` the nbsp/nnbsp chars are emitted as raw UTF-8 (verified by
  `od`: `302 240` and `342 200 257` bytes); French spacing is still inserted as raw chars.
- With `lang fr` + `input.clean false`: no spacing is added before punctuation, but
  pre-existing nbsp/nnbsp are still escaped (`~`, `\,`) and `!` still gains `{}`:
  `French: « test » nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct !{} ? : ;`
- In `lang en` the only clean effect visible is `!` → `!{}`… actually: en output was
  `punct !{} ? : ;` with nbsp→`~`, nnbsp→`\,`, no inserted spacing, guillemets untouched.
- babel line for fr: `\usepackage[francais]{babel} % Language support`.

## 10. Options: title/font/margins/paper/stdpage/hyperref/template.add/toc

- `tex.title false` → no `\maketitle` (grep count 0).
- `tex.font.size 11` → `\documentclass[11pt]{article}`; `12` → `[12pt]`. **No validation**:
  `--set tex.font.size 13` → `\documentclass[13pt]{article}` (exit 0, no warning) despite docs
  saying only 10/11/12. Non-integer aborts the render (empty stdout) with exit 0 and stderr:
  `ERROR Error in setting key tex.font.size: Error converting BookOption: expected an integer as value for key 'tex.font.size', found String("abc")`
- Margins (geometry line):
  - article (and any non-book class): `left=2cm,right=2cm`
  - book: `left=2.5cm,right=1.5cm`
  - both: `top=2cm, bottom=1.5cm`
  - `--set tex.margin.left 3cm tex.margin.top 5cm` →
    `\usepackage[a5paper, top=5cm, bottom=1.5cm,\n  left=3cm,right=2cm]{geometry} % Set dimensions/margins of the page`
- `tex.paper.size letterpaper` → `\usepackage[letterpaper, top=2cm, ...]{geometry}`.
- `tex.stdpage true` → replaces the margin geometry with:
```latex
\usepackage[a5paper]{geometry}
\usepackage[hyphen=false, parskip]{stdpage}
```
- `tex.template.add '\usepackage{foo}'` → inserted verbatim right before `\makeatother`.
- `tex.template mytemplate.tex` uses a custom mustache-ish template (`<<class>>`, `<<content>>`
  etc.); missing file aborts render (exit 0): `ERROR p.md: Could not find file '/nonexistent.tex' for template 'tex.template'`
- `tex.hyperref false`: see §8 (package still included).
- `rendering.inline_toc true` → `\tableofcontents` after `\maketitle`.
- Metadata: `title`/`author` → `\title{}`/`\author{}` + `\hypersetup{pdfauthor=...,pdftitle=...,
  pdfsubject={description}}`; `date` → `\date{2020-01-01}`.
- Cover: metadata key `cover: cover.pdf` + `tex.cover: true` (class book) → `\usepackage{pdfpages}`
  and inside `\maketitle`: `\includepdf{images/image_0.pdf}` (cover is renamed like an image).

## 11. `--to pdf` behavior and error paths (exact)

crowbook renders tex into a temp dir `/tmp/<32 lowercase hex chars>/result.tex`
(e.g. `/tmp/73e0f2216b98481fad2b421dd087062c`), then runs
`<tex.command> result.tex` **three times** in that cwd (verified with a logging fake command;
single argument, no extra flags). It then copies `result.pdf` byte-for-byte to the output
(`-o` file, or stdout when `-o` is omitted or `-o -`). The temp dir is deleted afterwards
(success and failure). If `-o` names a file, the pdf bytes land there; stdout stays empty.

### xelatex missing (default `tex.command: xelatex`)
Command: `--single p.md --to pdf -o out.pdf`
- stdout: empty
- stderr (verbatim):
```
CROWBOOK 0.17.0
ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'
```
- exit code: **0**; no `out.pdf` created. Same result with `-o -` and with no `-o`.

### `--set tex.command /bin/true` (runs OK but produces no pdf)
- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: could not open result of command '/bin/true'`
- exit 0, no output file.

### `--set tex.command /bin/false` (non-zero exit)
- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: /bin/false didn't return succesfully`
  (typo `succesfully` verbatim)
- exit 0, no output file.

### tex.command with arguments
`--set tex.command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'` — the whole string is treated as
the executable name (no word splitting):
`ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'`

### fake command that writes result.pdf
Script `for f in *.tex; do printf 'FAKEPDF' > "${f%.tex}.pdf"; done`:

## 2. tex.class: article vs book

- `--single` mode defaults to **article** (`\documentclass{article}`), even though
  `--list-options` says `tex.class` default is `book`. In book-config mode the class is `book`.
- `--set tex.class book` → `\documentclass{book}`.
- With `book`, the preamble additionally contains a `\renewcommand{\maketitle}{...}` block
  (fancy title page + copyright page, using `<<subtitle>>`, `<<version>>`, `<<license>>`,
  `<<autograph>>`); with any other class that block is absent (only the fancyhdr redefinition).
- Invalid class is passed through verbatim: `--set tex.class nonsense` → `\documentclass{nonsense}`
  (exit 0, no warning; the `book`-only maketitle block is then omitted).

## 3. Headers

Book class (`--set tex.class book`), input with `# H1` … `###### H6`:

```latex
\chapter{H1}
\label{chapter-0}
\section{H2}
\subsection{H3}
\subsubsection{H4}
\paragraoh{H5}
\paragraoh{H6}
```

Article class (default for `--single`), same input:

```latex
\section{H1}
\label{chapter-0}
\section{H2}
\subsection{H3}
\subsubsection{H4}
\paragraoh{H5}
\paragraoh{H6}
```

- **Bug (verbatim): H5 and H6 render as `\paragraoh{...}`** — a typo for `\paragraph` (both levels).
- In article class both H1 and H2 map to `\section` (chapter collapses onto section).
- `\label{chapter-N}` follows the first chapter header; N counts chapters AND parts (see §8).
- If the first header in a `--single` file is H2, it still becomes `\section{...}`.

### rendering.num_depth has NO effect on tex
Outputs for `rendering.num_depth` 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 are byte-identical (verified with `diff`,
both in `--single` and book-config mode). No starred/unstarred switching, no `secnumdepth`.
The only way to get starred commands is an unnumbered chapter (`-` prefix in the .book file):
then the chapter AND all its descendant headers are starred with `\addcontentsline`:

```latex
\section*{Chapter Two}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Chapter Two}
\label{chapter-1}
\section*{Sec}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Sec}
```
(book class: `\chapter*{...}` + `\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{...}`)

## 4. Inline markup

Input:
```

```

- `\mdstrong` = `\textbf`, `\mdcode` = `\texttt` (defined in preamble).
- Strikethrough uses `\sout`; `\usepackage[normalem]{ulem}` is included only when strike is used.
- `~sub~` also maps to `\sout{...}` (it IS the strikethrough syntax); `^sup^` is NOT supported —
  the carets are escaped: `Super \textasciicircum{}script\textasciicircum{} and sub \sout{script}.`
- Inline code escaping: `` `code $pecial #_chars` `` →
  `\mdcode{code \$pecial \#\_\allowbreak{}chars}` (note `\allowbreak{}` after `\_`).
- `rendering.initials true` → `\usepackage{lettrine}` and first paragraph of chapter starts
  `\lettrine{S}{ome} \emph{emphasis}, ...`.

## 6. Code blocks: syntect vs none

Default (`rendering.highlight: syntect`, theme `InspiredGitHub`): every fenced or indented block
becomes an `mdcodeblock` environment (mdframed) with per-token
`\textcolor[rgb]{r, g, b}{\texttt{...}}`, keywords additionally wrapped in `\textbf{...}`,
spaces as `\hphantom{ }\allowbreak{}`, `(`/`)` get `\allowbreak{}`, line end is `\\{}` and an
extra `\\{}` after the last line. Preamble gains `spverbatim`, `color`, `mdframed` packages and
the `mdcodeblock` env definition (only when the document contains code blocks).

Example (```rust fn main() { println!("hi"); } ```), abridged verbatim start:
```latex
\begin{mdcodeblock}
{\sloppy \textbf{\textcolor[rgb]{0.654902, 0.11372549, 0.3647059}{\texttt{fn}}}\textcolor[rgb]{0.19607843, 0.19607843, 0.19607843}{\texttt{\hphantom{ }\allowbreak{}}}...
\end{mdcodeblock}
```

- No language / unknown language → all tokens in default color `0.19607843, 0.19607843, 0.19607843`.
- Indented code blocks are highlighted too (as plain text).
- `rendering.highlight none` (or any unrecognized value, e.g. `bogus` — silently accepted) →
```latex
\begin{mdcodeblock}
\begin{spverbatim}
fn main() { println!("hi"); }

\end{spverbatim}
\end{mdcodeblock}
```
- Themes: `rendering.highlight.theme 'Solarized (dark)'` and `tex.highlight.theme 'Solarized (dark)'`
  both change the colors (identical results). Invalid theme name: document still renders with the
  default theme, exit 0, stderr:
```

WARNING Crowbook exited successfully, but the following errors occurred:
ERROR could not set syntect theme to NoSuchTheme, defaulting to "InspiredGitHub"
```

Input:

```
|:-----|:------:|------:|---------|
| a | b | c | d |

```
Output:
```latex

\hline
left & center & right & default\\

a & b & c & d\\ 

\hline
\end{mdtable}
```
