## 8. Links, images, parts, labels

Input (images must exist or the whole render aborts, see §10):
```
A [link to example](https://example.com) and [relative](page.html#anchor) and autolink <https://foo.bar/baz>.

[ref link][r]

[r]: https://ref.example "title"

An image: ![alt text](img.png) and standalone:

![alone](pic.jpg)
```
Output:
```latex
A \href{https://example.com}{link to example}\protect\footnote{\url{https://example.com}} and \href{page.html\#anchor}{relative}\protect\footnote{\url{page.html\#anchor}} and autolink \url{https://foo.bar/baz}.

\href{https://ref.example}{ref link}\protect\footnote{\url{https://ref.example}}

An image: \mdimage{images/image_0.png} and standalone:

\mdstandaloneimage{images/image_1.jpg}
```
- `tex.links_as_footnotes true` (default) appends `\protect\footnote{\url{...}}` after each
  `\href`; `false` omits it. Autolinks are plain `\url{...}` (never footnoted).
- **Local image files are renamed** in the tex to `images/image_N.<ext>` (N = 0-based order of
  appearance, cover included). `\mdstandaloneimage` = centered `\includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]`,
  `\mdimage` = bare `\includegraphics` (definitions in preamble, only included when images used).
- **Remote images (`https://...`) are silently dropped** — no warning even with `-v`.
- Anchor-only links like `[x](#chapter-1)` are NOT treated as internal:
  `\href{\#chapter-1}{x}\protect\footnote{\url{\#chapter-1}}`.

### Internal links (book config only) and tex.pageref_template
Book with `+ ch1.md` / `+ ch2.md`, link `[chapter two](ch2.md)`:
```latex
Go to \hyperref[chapter-1]{chapter two}\footnote{p\pageref{chapter-1}} and \hyperref[chapter-1]{anchor}\footnote{p\pageref{chapter-1}}.
```
- Default `tex.pageref_template` = `\footnote{p\pageref{<<key>>}}` (note: no `.` after `p`).
- `--set tex.pageref_template 'X<<key>>Y'` → `\hyperref[chapter-1]{chapter two}Xchapter-1Y`.
- `tex.hyperref false` → internal links are NOT resolved; they render as external:
  `\href{ch2.md}{chapter two}\protect\footnote{\url{ch2.md}}`. The `\usepackage{hyperref}` line
  stays in the preamble regardless (option only changes link resolution).

### Parts and chapter counters
Book-config part marker is `@` (line `@ Part One`). Output:
```latex
\setcounter{chapter}{0}\part{Part One}
\label{chapter-0}
\chapter{Chapter One}
\label{chapter-1}
```
- Parts get their own `\label{chapter-N}` (single counter shared with chapters).
- `\setcounter{chapter}{0}` is emitted per part (matches `rendering.part.reset_counter` default true).
- `! Part` is rejected: `ERROR p.book:2: Error parsing configuration file: error.chapter_whitespace`
  (untranslated error key, verbatim).
- `rendering.chapter Chapitre` / `rendering.part Livre` insert after `\begin{document}`:
```latex
\makeatletter
\renewcommand{\@chapapp}{Chapitre}
\makeatother

\renewcommand{\partname}{Livre}
```
- `rendering.chapter.roman_numerals` / `rendering.part.roman_numerals` /
  `rendering.chapter.template` / `rendering.part.template` produce NO change in the tex output
  (they only affect HTML/EPUB TOC naming; tex TOC is `\tableofcontents`).

## 9. Escaping, smart quotes, French typography, nbsp

Escaping input:
```
Special: # $ % & _ { } ~ ^ \ and < > |.

"quotes" and 'apostrophes' -- dashes --- ellipsis...
```
Output:
```latex
Special: \# \$ \% \& \_ \{ \} \textasciitilde{} \textasciicircum{} \textbackslash{} and \textless{} \textgreater{} |.

“quotes” and ‘apostrophes’ -{}- dashes -{}-{}- ellipsis...
```
- `|` is NOT escaped. `--` → `-{}-`, `---` → `-{}-{}-` (ligature breakers, not dashes).
- Smart quotes (default `input.clean.smart_quotes true`) produce literal UTF-8 curly quotes
  `“ ” ‘ ’`; with `--set input.clean.smart_quotes false` the ASCII quotes pass through.
- Unicode (é, 🎉, € …) passes through raw (preamble assumes xelatex/fontspec).
- Raw inline/block HTML is escaped as text: `<b>` → `\textless{}b\textgreater{}`.
- `input.clean.ligature.dashes true`: `--` → `–`, `---` → `—` (real UTF-8 dashes).
- `input.clean.ligature.guillemets true`: `<<d>>` → `«d»`.

### French (`--set lang fr`), input: `French: « test » nbsp:<NBSP>here nnbsp:<NNBSP>here punct ! ? : ;`
With default `tex.escape_nb_spaces true`:
```latex
French: «\,test\,» nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct\,!{}\,?~:\,;
```
- U+00A0 (nbsp) → `~`, U+202F (narrow nbsp) → `\,`.
- French auto-clean (`input.clean` default true) inserts narrow nbsp before `! ? ;` (→ `\,!{}`,
  `\,?`, `\,;` — note `!` also gains `{}`) and nbsp before `:` (→ `~:`); spaces inside `« »`
  become narrow nbsp (→ `«\,test\,»`).
- With `tex.escape_nb_spaces false` the nbsp/nnbsp chars are emitted as raw UTF-8 (verified by
  `od`: `302 240` and `342 200 257` bytes); French spacing is still inserted as raw chars.
- With `lang fr` + `input.clean false`: no spacing is added before punctuation, but
  pre-existing nbsp/nnbsp are still escaped (`~`, `\,`) and `!` still gains `{}`:
  `French: « test » nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct !{} ? : ;`
- In `lang en` the only clean effect visible is `!` → `!{}`… actually: en output was
  `punct !{} ? : ;` with nbsp→`~`, nnbsp→`\,`, no inserted spacing, guillemets untouched.
- babel line for fr: `\usepackage[francais]{babel} % Language support`.

## 10. Options: title/font/margins/paper/stdpage/hyperref/template.add/toc

- `tex.title false` → no `\maketitle` (grep count 0).
- `tex.font.size 11` → `\documentclass[11pt]{article}`; `12` → `[12pt]`. **No validation**:
  `--set tex.font.size 13` → `\documentclass[13pt]{article}` (exit 0, no warning) despite docs
  saying only 10/11/12. Non-integer aborts the render (empty stdout) with exit 0 and stderr:
  `ERROR Error in setting key tex.font.size: Error converting BookOption: expected an integer as value for key 'tex.font.size', found String("abc")`
- Margins (geometry line):
  - article (and any non-book class): `left=2cm,right=2cm`
  - book: `left=2.5cm,right=1.5cm`
  - both: `top=2cm, bottom=1.5cm`
  - `--set tex.margin.left 3cm tex.margin.top 5cm` →
    `\usepackage[a5paper, top=5cm, bottom=1.5cm,\n  left=3cm,right=2cm]{geometry} % Set dimensions/margins of the page`
- `tex.paper.size letterpaper` → `\usepackage[letterpaper, top=2cm, ...]{geometry}`.
- `tex.stdpage true` → replaces the margin geometry with:
```latex
\usepackage[a5paper]{geometry}
\usepackage[hyphen=false, parskip]{stdpage}
```
- `tex.template.add '\usepackage{foo}'` → inserted verbatim right before `\makeatother`.
- `tex.template mytemplate.tex` uses a custom mustache-ish template (`<<class>>`, `<<content>>`
  etc.); missing file aborts render (exit 0): `ERROR p.md: Could not find file '/nonexistent.tex' for template 'tex.template'`
- `tex.hyperref false`: see §8 (package still included).
- `rendering.inline_toc true` → `\tableofcontents` after `\maketitle`.
- Metadata: `title`/`author` → `\title{}`/`\author{}` + `\hypersetup{pdfauthor=...,pdftitle=...,
  pdfsubject={description}}`; `date` → `\date{2020-01-01}`.
- Cover: metadata key `cover: cover.pdf` + `tex.cover: true` (class book) → `\usepackage{pdfpages}`
  and inside `\maketitle`: `\includepdf{images/image_0.pdf}` (cover is renamed like an image).

## 11. `--to pdf` behavior and error paths (exact)

crowbook renders tex into a temp dir `/tmp/<32 lowercase hex chars>/result.tex`
(e.g. `/tmp/73e0f2216b98481fad2b421dd087062c`), then runs
`<tex.command> result.tex` **three times** in that cwd (verified with a logging fake command;
single argument, no extra flags). It then copies `result.pdf` byte-for-byte to the output
(`-o` file, or stdout when `-o` is omitted or `-o -`). The temp dir is deleted afterwards
(success and failure). If `-o` names a file, the pdf bytes land there; stdout stays empty.

### xelatex missing (default `tex.command: xelatex`)
Command: `--single p.md --to pdf -o out.pdf`
- stdout: empty
- stderr (verbatim):
```
CROWBOOK 0.17.0
ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'
```
- exit code: **0**; no `out.pdf` created. Same result with `-o -` and with no `-o`.

### `--set tex.command /bin/true` (runs OK but produces no pdf)
- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: could not open result of command '/bin/true'`
- exit 0, no output file.

### `--set tex.command /bin/false` (non-zero exit)
- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: /bin/false didn't return succesfully`
  (typo `succesfully` verbatim)
- exit 0, no output file.

### tex.command with arguments
`--set tex.command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'` — the whole string is treated as
the executable name (no word splitting):
`ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'`

### fake command that writes result.pdf
Script `for f in *.tex; do printf 'FAKEPDF' > "${f%.tex}.pdf"; done`:
- invoked exactly 3× as `faketex.sh result.tex`, cwd = temp dir
- exit 0; stderr only `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` (no success message)
- `-o fake.pdf` → file contains exactly `FAKEPDF`; with `-o -` or no `-o`, `FAKEPDF` goes to stdout.

### missing output directory
`--to pdf -o nodir/out.pdf` (command succeeded):
`ERROR could not create file 'nodir/out.pdf': 'No such file or directory (os error 2)`
(note the unbalanced quote before `No such`; exit 0)

Report written to `/workspace/ref/reports/epub.md` (~1100 lines, all EPUB file contents quoted verbatim). Key findings: **Archive structure** — fixed order: `mimetype` (first, STORED, exact bytes `application/epub+zip`, no newline), `META-INF/container.xml`, `META-INF/com.apple.ibooks.display-options.xml`, then `[cover.xhtml,] title_page.xhtml, chapter_NNN.xhtml…, stylesheet.css, images/data…, content.opf, toc.ncx, nav.xhtml`. `container.xml` and the iBooks file are byte-identical constants. `toc.ncx` and `nav.xhtml` are emitted in **both** epub.version 2 and 3. **Chapter naming** — `chapter_{:03}.xhtml`, one sequence covering chapters *and* parts (parts come from `@ Title` lines in the `.book` file and get their own xhtml). `-` files are unnumbered but still in spine/TOC; nothing is ever truly hidden. Multiple `#` chapters in one md file merge into one xhtml with a warning containing an unsubstituted literal `{source}`. **Metadata / OPF** — `dc:identifier` is `urn:uuid:` + a **random v4 UUID, different every run**; `dcterms:modified` (v3 only) is run time, not the `date` option (`date` and `version` are never emitted). `dc:description` is inserted **raw without XML escaping** (invalid XML with `&`). v3 has a duplicate-id bug: `dc:language` gets `id="epub-creator-0"`, same as `dc:creator`. v2 vs v3 differ in doctype (XHTML 1.1 vs HTML5), chapter wrapper (`
` vs `
`), `opf:role="aut"` vs id+refines, and nav landmarks (v3 only). **TOC** — `playOrder` sequential; part children nested with `#link-N` anchors; NCX labels of nested items drop their numbers ("Third") while nav.xhtml keeps them ("1. Third"); `dtb:depth` hardcoded `1` even when nested. `epub.toc.extras: false` drops Cover/Title from NCX/nav/landmarks and empties their `` titles. **zip fallback** — crowbook probes with `zip -v` in a temp dir (`/tmp/.tmpXXXXXX`, left behind empty); on spawn failure or non-zero exit it warns `Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library` and uses the Rust zip crate. Otherwise it runs `zip -X0 output.epub mimetype` then `zip -9 output.epub `. Exact `-n` mode text: `[WARN] Could not run zip command, falling back to zip library` / `[INFO] Succesfully generated EPUB: nf.epub` (typo "Succesfully"). **escape_nb_spaces** (fr) — U+202F runs become `… …`; standalone U+00A0 before `:` stays a raw literal. **Notable robustness bugs** — almost all errors (missing image → no EPUB written, broken temp epub, bad option) still exit **0**, and a missing image prints "exited successfully" while producing no file. Only argument-parser errors exit non-zero (exit 2).

payload.resultSummary:
Report written to `/workspace/ref/reports/markdown-html.md` (839 lines, all test inputs + verbatim outputs + exit codes). Compact summary of the most important findings: **Document structure** - `--single` puts all chapters in one `
`; book mode gives each file its own `chapter-N` div. Chapter h1 = `

Chapter N
Title

` (single quotes, from `html.chapter.template`). - IDs: `link-0` is always the book-title h1; all headings of any level then take sequential `link-N`. Paragraphs get one global `para-N` counter (including inside quotes/lists/footnotes); `

` has no id. **Rendering quirks** - Strong = `` (not ``); `~~x~~` = `` by default; HRs render as `

***

`, never `
`. - Default syntect highlighting: `
` with per-line `…` (InspiredGitHub), no `` wrapper, trailing blank line; unknown/no lang = plain-colored spans, still escaped. With `rendering.highlight none`/`highlight.js`: `
` but content is **not HTML-escaped** (raw `<`/`&` leak).
- `crowbook.html_as_text` (default true) escapes *all* HTML to text (and smart-quotes it); with false, HTML blocks are **dropped entirely** (not passed through), inline tags stripped keeping inner text.
- Entities like `©` are decoded to raw `©`; named `©` too; unknown entities escaped.
- Tables: alignment info is discarded; wrapped in `
`. Lists: different bullet chars split lists; `5.` start numbers ignored (no `start` attr, merges with previous `
    `); tight lists still wrap `
  1. ` content in `
    `.
- Images embedded as base64 data URIs (`title = ""` when absent); standalone image paragraph → `
    `. Missing image → `ERROR … for image` on stderr, exit 0, **empty stdout**.
- Footnotes: refs `[name]` where F = 1-based source-file index; repeated refs duplicate the same id; notes end in `
    ` with a backlink ``; ordered by first reference; `^[inline]` unsupported.
- `rendering.num_depth` 0/1/2/3/6 → none / chapters only / `1.1.` / `2.0.1.` / down to h6. Hidden chapters (`- file`) and their subsections are never numbered. Parts via `@ Title` lines in the .book → `
    Part I
    Title
    `; roman numerals and chapter-counter reset on by default.

**Cleaning/typography**
- Smart quotes (default on): straight → curly, `'` → `’`, unbalanced closing `"` falls back to opening `“`. `input.clean false` also disables multi-space collapse.
- French (`lang fr`, also via YAML block): only *existing* spaces are converted — before `! ? ; % €` and inside `« »` → **U+202F**, before `:` → **U+00A0**; nothing is ever inserted (`Bonjour!` untouched). Quirk: `«…»` at paragraph start gets U+00A0 inside, mid-sentence gets U+202F. French also turns `...` into `…` and adds U+00A0 around dashes (English does neither). `html.escape_nb_spaces true` (default) wraps each U+202F group as `word !`; U+00A0 stays a raw byte.
- Ligature options (default off): `--`→`–`, `---`→`—` (greedy, `----`→`—-`); `<<`/`>>`→`«`/`»`. `crowbook.markdown.superscript true`: `^x^`→``, `~x~`→``; with it off, `~x~` is strikethrough.
- `rendering.initials true` adds `class = "first-para"` to the first paragraph of each chapter. `rendering.inline_toc true` inserts `
    Table of contents
      …` listing only chapters, numbered per `rendering.chapter.template`; name localizes ("Table des matières" in French).
- Top-of-file YAML metadata block is always parsed in single mode (sets title/author/lang/any option; `input.yaml_blocks` had no observable effect — mid-document `---` blocks are never parsed).

**Security-relevant**: ``, ld+json `"name"`/`"author"`, and `html.header`/`html.footer` values are emitted **unescaped** (raw `<`, `&`, `"` — breaks JSON); the body title h1 *is* escaped.

Report written to `/workspace/ref/reports/tex.md` (574 lines, all verbatim outputs included). Compact summary of key findings:

**Rendering highlights**
- `--single` defaults to **article** class despite `tex.class` default being documented as `book`; book-config mode uses `book`. Only `book` gets the fancy `\maketitle` redefinition.
- Header mapping (book): H1→`\chapter`, H2→`\section`, H3→`\subsection`, H4→`\subsubsection`, **H5/H6→`\paragraoh` (typo bug, verbatim)**. Article: both H1 and H2→`\section`. Every chapter/part gets `\label{chapter-N}` from one shared counter, even headerless `--single` files (`\label{chapter-0}`).
- **`rendering.num_depth` has zero effect on tex** (byte-identical output for 0–6). Starred commands (`\chapter*`/`\section*` + `\addcontentsline`) only come from `-` unnumbered chapters, and propagate to descendant headers.
- Parts use `@ Title` in the .book file → `\setcounter{chapter}{0}\part{...}`; `!` fails with untranslated `error.chapter_whitespace`. `rendering.chapter/part` set `\@chapapp`/`\partname`; roman-numeral and `*.template` options do nothing in tex.
- Tables ignore alignment (always `{|X|X|…|}` tabularx); footnotes → `\footnotemark[N]`+`\footnotetext[N]{}`; links → `\href` + `\protect\footnote{\url{…}}` (default `links_as_footnotes true`); internal book links → `\hyperref[chapter-N]{…}\footnote{p\pageref{chapter-N}}` honoring `tex.pageref_template`. `tex.hyperref false` only disables internal resolution — hyperref package stays.
- Images renamed to `images/image_N.ext`; remote images silently dropped; missing local image aborts the whole render. Standalone images use `width=0.8\linewidth`.
- Escaping: `\# \$ \% \& \_ \{ \} \textasciitilde{} \textasciicircum{} \textbackslash{} \textless{} \textgreater{}`, but `|` unescaped; `--`→`-{}-`; smart quotes → literal UTF-8 curly quotes. French: nbsp→`~`, nnbsp→`\,` (with `escape_nb_spaces true`), auto-inserts `\,!{}` `\,?` `~:` `\,;` and `«\,…\,»`.
- `tex.font.size` unvalidated (`13pt` accepted); margins: article `2cm/2cm`, book `2.5cm/1.5cm`, top `2cm`, bottom `1.5cm`; paper default `a5paper`.

**PDF paths (all exit 0 despite errors)**
- Temp dir `/tmp/<32 hex>/result.tex`, command run **3×** as `<tex.command> result.tex` (no arg splitting — a command string with spaces fails), then `result.pdf` copied verbatim to `-o` or stdout (default output is stdout); temp dir always cleaned up.
- Missing xelatex: stderr exactly `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'` (with quotes), stdout empty, exit 0.
- `/bin/true` → `could not open result of command '/bin/true'`; `/bin/false` → `/bin/false didn't return succesfully` (typo verbatim).
- Only clap/usage errors exit 2; every runtime `ERROR` exits 0.

args.command:
cd /tmp/probe/htmldir && R=/workspace/ref/reports/html-dir.md && cat > $R <<'REPORT_EOF' # AREA REPORT: multifile HTML (`html.dir`) and misc HTML outputs Binary: `/workspace/executable` = crowbook 0.17.0. Scratch dir: `/tmp/probe/htmldir`. All commands run with stdout/stderr captured separately. Unless noted otherwise, commands were run non-interactively (no TTY), which matters (see "UI modes" below). ## 0. Global conventions observed - On startup the banner `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` is printed to **stderr** (except with `-q`). - Diagnostics in non-TTY mode go to **stderr**, prefixed `ERROR `, `[ERROR] `, `[WARN] `, `[INFO] `. Note two different error prefixes: `ERROR ` (logger) vs `[ERROR] ` (non-fancy UI error), and `INFO`/`WARN` only ever appear with brackets: `[INFO] `, `[WARN] `. - **Almost all errors exit with code 0.** Observed non-zero exit codes only for: - clap CLI parse errors (e.g. invalid `--to` value): exit 2 - internal panics (see bugs below): exit 101 - Success/info messages `[INFO] Succesfully generated ...` are only printed in non-TTY mode (with or without `-n`). On a TTY a fancy progress UI (spinner + progress bar) is shown and success is reported as `V : generated ` plus `V Finished`. - `-q` suppresses the banner and `[INFO]` messages, but NOT `ERROR` messages. ## 1. Test books used `ch1.md`: `# Chapter One\n\nText of chapter one.\n` (same pattern for ch2/ch3). `hid.md`: `# Hidden Chapter\n\nHidden chapter text.\n` `icon.png`: 8-byte fake PNG (`\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n`). book.book (3 numbered chapters, no icon): ``` title: Probe Book author: Jane Doe lang: en output.html.dir: out + ch1.md + ch2.md + ch3.md ``` book_icon.book = same + `html.icon: icon.png`, output `out_icon`. book_hidden.book: `+ ch1.md`, `- hid.md`, `+ ch3.md`, icon set, output `out_hid`. book_parts.book: `@ Part One`, `+ ch1.md`, `+ ch2.md`, `@ Part Two`, `+ ch3.md`, icon set, output `out_parts`. ## 2. `--to html.dir`: directory structure created With icon set (book_icon.book), stderr: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (multiple pages): out_icon ``` (exit 0, stdout empty) `out_icon/` contents (exactly these, nothing more): ``` chapter_000.html chapter_001.html chapter_002.html images/image_0.png <- only when html.icon and/or markdown images are used index.html menu.svg print.css stylesheet.css ``` Notes: - Filenames are `chapter_%03d.html` (zero-padded to 3 digits), numbered sequentially over ALL book items: parts AND hidden chapters each get their own file too. - The index page is always `index.html`. - `stylesheet.css` = default HTML CSS (base CSS + colors CSS concatenated); `print.css` = print stylesheet; `menu.svg` = the hamburger menu icon (2694 bytes, Inkscape SVG). - With `rendering.highlight: highlight.js`, two extra files are copied: `highlight.css`, `highlight.js` (and the template then links them). With default `syntect`, no extra files (code is pre-colored with inline styles). - Write order on error (see bug below) shows: chapter files, then `stylesheet.css`/`print.css`, then `index.html`, then `menu.svg`. ### Chapter file naming with parts and hidden chapters book_parts.book (2 parts, 3 chapters) produced 5 files: ``` chapter_000.html Probe Book - 1. Part One (part 1 page) chapter_001.html Probe Book - 1. Chapter One chapter_002.html Probe Book - 2. Chapter Two chapter_003.html Probe Book - 3. Part Two (part 2 page) chapter_004.html Probe Book - 1. Chapter Three ``` book_hidden.book (`+ ch1`, `- hid`, `+ ch3`) produced 3 files; the hidden chapter gets `chapter_001.html` with `Probe Book - Hidden Chapter` and an unnumbered heading `

Hidden Chapter

`. The following chapter is renumbered ("2. Chapter Three"). QUIRK: in `` and in prev/next link texts, a part is referenced by its sequential chapter-file number, not its roman numeral: `<title>Probe Book - 3. Part Two` and link text `3. Part Two »`, while the TOC entry is `II. Part Two` and the part page heading is `

Part II

`. ## 3. BUG: rendering fails without `html.icon` Running `--to html.dir` on book.book (no `html.icon`): - stdout: empty; stderr (verbatim): ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 ERROR Error compiling template: render error --> :8:7 | 8 | {{favicon}} | ^^^^^^^ | = reason: not found in this scope ``` - exit code 0. - Result: chapter_000..002.html, print.css, stylesheet.css ARE written (chapter pages render fine with an empty favicon line), but `index.html`, `menu.svg` and `images/` are MISSING. So the `{{favicon}}` template variable is defined for chapter pages but not for the index page render context; the index render error aborts the remaining output. - Standalone `--to html` does NOT have this bug (favicon line renders empty). Same render but WITHOUT `--to` (i.e. `crowbook book.book`) gives a differently wrapped message (still exit 0): ``` [ERROR] Error rendering html.dir: Error compiling template: render error ``` With `-L fr`: ``` [ERROR] Erreur dans le rendu de html.dir: Erreur dans la compilation du template : render error ``` ## 4. BUG: `--to html.dir` with `-o/--output` panics when `output.html.dir` is not set in the book `/workspace/executable --to html.dir --output outdir book.book` (book without `output.html.dir`): exit code **101**, stderr verbatim: ``` CROWBOOK 0.17.0 thread 'main' (6313) panicked at src/lib/html_dir.rs:464:64: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Error { source: Source { file: Some("book.book"), line: Some(4) }, inner: InvalidOption("option 'output.html.dir' is not present") } note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace ``` It creates the (empty) output directory first, then panics. Same panic in `--single` mode (`-s --to html.dir ch1.md -o sdir`, with `file: None, line: None`). If `output.html.dir` is already set in the book file, `-o otherdir` works normally (overrides the path). `-o -` does not panic (stream error instead, see below). (Note also: `--set` eats all following args as a list — `--set output.html.dir outdir book.book` consumes `book.book` and then errors `ERROR You must pass the name of a book configuration file. For more information try --help.`; you must use `--set k v -- book.book`.) ## 5. Rendered output sent "to stdout" and `--stats` tables go to **stdout**. - Almost every runtime error (config parse errors, missing files, render failures) still exits with **exit code 0**. Only CLI argument (clap) errors exit non-zero (**exit 2**). A self-import loop aborts with SIGABRT (exit 134). - Two error prefixes coexist: - `[ERROR] ...` — bracketed logger form (also `[WARN]`, `[INFO]`) - `ERROR ...` — plain form (used for fatal-ish top-level errors). Both still exit 0. - Typo preserved verbatim: `Succesfully` in all success messages, and `didn't return succesfully` for PDF. Success messages (verbatim, stderr): ``` [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page): book.html [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (multiple pages): hdir2 [INFO] Succesfully generated EPUB: custom.epub [INFO] Succesfully generated LaTeX: named.tex ``` When output goes to stdout (no file), the filename is omitted: ``` [INFO] Succesfully generated HTML (standalone page) [INFO] Succesfully generated LaTeX ``` ## .book config file syntax - One `key: value` per line. **Each option line is parsed as YAML** (the whole line, apparently as a one-line YAML document; keys with dots map to nested options). Value types accepted: strings (quoted or bare), booleans (ONLY `true`/`false`), integers, YAML lists (`[a, b]` or block `- item` style). - `#` starts a comment (full-line, or trailing after whitespace — standard YAML rules). `title: Foo #bar` yields title `Foo`. - Quoting: `"Quoted Title # not comment"` and `'Single Quoted'` both work. - Multiline values work via YAML: a double-quoted string spanning two lines, and folded style (`description: >-` followed by indented lines) are accepted. - Leading spaces before a key are OK (` title: Indented` worked). - **Duplicate keys: last one wins, no warning** (`title: First` then `title: Second` → `Second`). - Blank lines are ignored. - Empty config file (0 bytes) → fatal: ``` ERROR syn5.book: Error parsing configuration file: "could not parse %{file} as a book file." Maybe you meant to run crowbook with the --single argument? ``` (Note the literal `%{file}` — an unsubstituted placeholder bug. 447	## 9. Escaping, smart quotes, French typography, nbsp
448	
449	Escaping input:
450	```
451	Special: # $ % & _ { } ~ ^ \ and < > |.
452	
453	"quotes" and 'apostrophes' -- dashes --- ellipsis...
454	```
455	Output:
456	```latex
457	Special: \# \$ \% \& \_ \{ \} \textasciitilde{} \textasciicircum{} \textbackslash{} and \textless{} \textgreater{} |.
458	
459	“quotes” and ‘apostrophes’ -{}- dashes -{}-{}- ellipsis...
460	```
461	- `|` is NOT escaped. `--` → `-{}-`, `---` → `-{}-{}-` (ligature breakers, not dashes).
462	- Smart quotes (default `input.clean.smart_quotes true`) produce literal UTF-8 curly quotes
463	  `“ ” ‘ ’`; with `--set input.clean.smart_quotes false` the ASCII quotes pass through.
464	- Unicode (é, 🎉, € …) passes through raw (preamble assumes xelatex/fontspec).
465	- Raw inline/block HTML is escaped as text: `<b>` → `\textless{}b\textgreater{}`.
466	- `input.clean.ligature.dashes true`: `--` → `–`, `---` → `—` (real UTF-8 dashes).
467	- `input.clean.ligature.guillemets true`: `<<d>>` → `«d»`.
468	
469	### French (`--set lang fr`), input: `French: « test » nbsp:<NBSP>here nnbsp:<NNBSP>here punct ! ? : ;`
470	With default `tex.escape_nb_spaces true`:
471	```latex
472	French: «\,test\,» nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct\,!{}\,?~:\,;
473	```
474	- U+00A0 (nbsp) → `~`, U+202F (narrow nbsp) → `\,`.
475	- French auto-clean (`input.clean` default true) inserts narrow nbsp before `! ? ;` (→ `\,!{}`,
476	  `\,?`, `\,;` — note `!` also gains `{}`) and nbsp before `:` (→ `~:`); spaces inside `« »`
477	  become narrow nbsp (→ `«\,test\,»`).
478	- With `tex.escape_nb_spaces false` the nbsp/nnbsp chars are emitted as raw UTF-8 (verified by
479	  `od`: `302 240` and `342 200 257` bytes); French spacing is still inserted as raw chars.
480	- With `lang fr` + `input.clean false`: no spacing is added before punctuation, but
481	  pre-existing nbsp/nnbsp are still escaped (`~`, `\,`) and `!` still gains `{}`:
482	  `French: « test » nbsp:~here nnbsp:\,here punct !{} ? : ;`
483	- In `lang en` the only clean effect visible is `!` → `!{}`… actually: en output was
484	  `punct !{} ? : ;` with nbsp→`~`, nnbsp→`\,`, no inserted spacing, guillemets untouched.
485	- babel line for fr: `\usepackage[francais]{babel} % Language support`.

516	## 11. `--to pdf` behavior and error paths (exact)
517	
518	crowbook renders tex into a temp dir `/tmp/<32 lowercase hex chars>/result.tex`
519	(e.g. `/tmp/73e0f2216b98481fad2b421dd087062c`), then runs
520	`<tex.command> result.tex` **three times** in that cwd (verified with a logging fake command;
521	single argument, no extra flags). It then copies `result.pdf` byte-for-byte to the output
522	(`-o` file, or stdout when `-o` is omitted or `-o -`). The temp dir is deleted afterwards
523	(success and failure). If `-o` names a file, the pdf bytes land there; stdout stays empty.
524	
525	### xelatex missing (default `tex.command: xelatex`)
526	Command: `--single p.md --to pdf -o out.pdf`
527	- stdout: empty
528	- stderr (verbatim):
529	```
530	CROWBOOK 0.17.0
531	ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command 'xelatex'
532	```
533	- exit code: **0**; no `out.pdf` created. Same result with `-o -` and with no `-o`.
534	
535	### `--set tex.command /bin/true` (runs OK but produces no pdf)
536	- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: could not open result of command '/bin/true'`
537	- exit 0, no output file.
538	
539	### `--set tex.command /bin/false` (non-zero exit)
540	- stderr: `ERROR Error during temporary files editing: /bin/false didn't return succesfully`
541	  (typo `succesfully` verbatim)
542	- exit 0, no output file.
543	
544	### tex.command with arguments
545	`--set tex.command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'` — the whole string is treated as
546	the executable name (no word splitting):
547	`ERROR Error during temporary files editing: failed to run command '/path/faketex.sh --interaction=nonstopmode'`
548	
549	### fake command that writes result.pdf
550	Script `for f in *.tex; do printf 'FAKEPDF' > "${f%.tex}.pdf"; done`:
551	- invoked exactly 3× as `faketex.sh result.tex`, cwd = temp dir
552	- exit 0; stderr only `CROWBOOK 0.17.0` (no success message)
553	- `-o fake.pdf` → file contains exactly `FAKEPDF`; with `-o -` or no `-o`, `FAKEPDF` goes to stdout.
554	
555	### missing output directory
556	`--to pdf -o nodir/out.pdf` (command succeeded):
557	`ERROR could not create file 'nodir/out.pdf': 'No such file or directory (os error 2)`
558	(note the unbalanced quote before `No such`; exit 0)
